newsitem.title: THAILAND: GOLF-TIGER TAMED BY HIGH THAI TEMPERATURES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER TAMED BY HIGH THAI TEMPERATURES.

text.p: Thailand's heat proved too much for Tiger Woods on Wednesday, forcing the current sensation of world golf to withdraw from a pro-am tournament after 13 holes.
"It's heat exhaustion," said Peter German, tournament director for the Asian Honda Classic which begins on Thursday. "He's not a well boy."
German said Woods had decided to pull out when temperatures of 33 degrees celsius proved too much.
The American, who has a Thai mother, is still expected to tee off on Thursday morning in the main tournament -- his first professional event in Asia.

Woods also failed to appear at a news conference he was due to give on Wednesday afternoon. "He has just come off playing in Pebble Beach, then he got on a plane and arrived last night. He is exhausted," German said.
Until his abrupt retirement, Woods was followed by a crowd of excited fans as he played in the late morning heat under a scorching sun.
His nationally televised arrival at the airport late on Thursday was similar to that of a movie star as dozens of excited fans waited to greet their "native son".

Wearing several traditional Thai flower garlands around his neck, Woods looked surprised to see the hoards of media covering his arrival as he stood next to his mother and tried to make his way through the crowds to his car.
Tiger frenzy has hit Bangkok over the past few days as Thais prepared to welcome Woods.
Although the 21-year-old has only been to Thailand three times and speaks virtually nothing of the language, Thai people consider him to be one of their own.
Woods' mother has become a local media celebrity over the past week and delighted many young Thai women by saying she hoped her son would follow in his father's footsteps and marry a Thai woman.
A plan to grant Woods honorary Thai citizenship was scrapped because of the problems it would cause with his American citizenship, tournament organisers said.

Woods, who is reportedly receiving $500,000 to compete in Thursday's tournament -- which has a $300,000 purse -- will be competing against other top pros like Steve Elkington, Frank Nobilo and Curtis Strange.
